| [QUESTION-378](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-378.md) | Under what conditions does coupling two locally rigid organizational subsystems create new adaptive degrees of freedom at their interface? | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched), Part 5. The readings answer the mechanical version only under conditions, and the question is asked with them. A flexible interface between rigid kirigami needs the two sides in topologically distinct phases, and the opposite pairing or orientation gives a stressed line instead (Chen et al.; Kane and Lubensky). A link joining two components of a linkage removes three rigid-body freedoms and adds one internal one (Chen, Choi and Mahadevan). Decoupled units in series add nothing new (Jules et al.). So coupling rigid parts does not in general create freedom. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |

The record holds that viability does not settle what ought to persist ([CLAIM-075](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md)), that a normative judgment is well-defined once its relata are fixed ([CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md)), and asks whether the standards themselves can be objective ([QUESTION-129](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md)); none asks what grounds the authority of a relationship, capability or restriction as distinct from its adequacy. A71's survey of answers, a triad of legitimacy, adequacy and efficacy and five candidate sources, is carried in the body as A's. | Open |
| [QUESTION-486](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-486.md) v2 | Can rights that no institution creates or can extinguish, the Founders' "unalienable rights", serve as the institution-independent criteria the record's normative judgments of organizations need, and what would such rights have to be to do so? | The owner's, from U37 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-17): "what if we leverage the Founders' notion of "inalienable rights" as independent normative criteria to build on?" A proposal put as a question. The record's judgments of organizations are relative to a standard declared with each judgment ([CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md)), and how such a standard can be objective, or the demand set established defensibly, is open ([QUESTION-129](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md), [QUESTION-456](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-456.md)). The owner proposes a source of standards that is independent of any institution by construction. A85 takes it up ("your suggestion identifies a valuable way forward"); its reconstruction of inalienability is filed as [CLAIM-720](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-720.md). The adopted Declaration reads "unalienable". | Open |
| [QUESTION-487](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-487.md) v2 | What lets those who act for an organization hold the principals who direct them accountable for the conditions under which they are required to act, and does any principal–agent account carry accountability in that reverse direction? | A's, from the close of A17 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-15): "Traditional principal–agent models ask how principals can ensure that agents act in their interests. These two concepts suggest the inverse question: *How can agents hold principals accountable for the conditions under which agents are required to act?*" A offered it as "the foundation of a fairly general theory of organizational moral exploitation" and did not take it further. It sharpens [QUESTION-461](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md)'s second branch to the instruments that would turn an agent's indispensable effort into a claim on the conditions it works under. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
